clue.text: Masterstrokes up among the lettuce

indicators.note: among says one piece is set in the midst of the other, here the word up placed inside

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce (romaine)
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something clever has been planted in the lettuce bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal; 'up' looks like part of a phrase but is taken literally, and cos is the long-leaved lettuce also called romaine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a brilliant, successful stroke or move.

clue.text: Wagnerian heroine is elderly in an archaic way

parts.note: taken as written
olde is the mock-antique spelling of old, as in 'ye olde'

explanation.surface: A remark that one of Wagner's leading ladies is getting on and speaks quaintly.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: Exchanging part of dockland nearest the Surrey side

indicators.note: nearest says the first piece stands right next to the second, at its front

parts.note: the Surrey side of the Thames is the south bank, so S for south
Wapping is a district of London's Docklands

explanation.surface: Trading places in a stretch of the London docks close to the south bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping lies on the north bank of the Thames in East London; Surrey borders the river's south bank, so 'the Surrey side' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping is trading one thing for another, the same as exchanging.

clue.text: Fellows following me to provide a souvenir

indicators.note: following says the men come after the me in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
fellows are men
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of men trailing after the speaker to hand over a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is a positional signal: the fellows come after 'me' in the answer, not before it as in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder, a keepsake.

clue.text: Stately home where orange becomes apple

definitions.text: Stately home where orange becomes apple

parts.words: Stately home where orange becomes apple
parts.note: a famous Oxfordshire palace whose name, followed by the word orange, names a variety of dessert apple

explanation.surface: A grand country house where citrus fruit turns into orchard fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is the Duke of Marlborough's seat in Oxfordshire; the Blenheim Orange is an old English apple variety, so here 'orange' is the name of an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim is both a famous stately home and the first word of an apple's name.

clue.text: Quarters for itinerant campanologists?

parts.note: touring bell-ringers would naturally lodge in canvas shelters named after their bells

explanation.surface: Asking where travelling bell-ringers might stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers; a bell tent is a conical tent with a single central pole, and the name is read as tents for bell people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tents are temporary quarters for travellers, and these carry the ringers' instrument in their name.

clue.text: Booked as boy hero with most weary disposition

indicators.note: disposition, in the sense of arrangement, says the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A tired-out boy, the hero of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but means arrangement: the letters of MOST WEARY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel, so a hero in a book.

clue.text: Depressed state of the Royal Horse Guards

definitions.meaning: the British cavalry regiment nicknamed for its blue tunics

explanation.surface: Wondering about the morale of a smart cavalry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Horse Guards were known as 'The Blues' (now the Blues and Royals, part of the Household Cavalry).
explanation.definitionFit: The word means melancholy and is also the cavalry regiment's nickname.

clue.text: Confession of inability? Utter hypocrisy!

definitions.meaning: saying one is unable, as in 'I cannot', run together without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are not up to it, and is accused of rank insincerity.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is CAN'T with the apostrophe dropped; the second is cant, sanctimonious talk.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the admission 'cannot'; the other is insincere moralising talk.

clue.text: With order to follow, the caterer finds it perfect

definitions.text: With order to follow, the caterer finds it perfect

parts.words: With order to follow, the caterer finds it perfect
parts.note: a dessert a caterer might serve which, when the word order is put after it, makes a phrase for perfect neatness

explanation.surface: A caterer praising a well-run kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple-pie order' means perfect tidiness, while apple pie itself is a caterer's dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is a pudding, and before 'order' it means everything in perfect arrangement.

clue.text: Ronald disturbed by Tom Brown's doctor

indicators.note: disturbed suggests letters knocked out of their order and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A boy called Ronald upset by the headmaster in a school story.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Thomas Arnold was headmaster of Rugby School and appears in the novel Tom Brown's Schooldays.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Arnold is the famous headmaster in Tom Brown's Schooldays.

clue.text: Oriental sprite for each one in Rome

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mischievous Eastern spirit handing out one apiece in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy-like being in Persian mythology.

clue.text: Tied up with Edward about there

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bound up with Edward somewhere over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around: Edward's short form is split open to hold 'there', and 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied with a rope, as an animal to a post.

clue.text: Express transport apparently without a dining car

definitions.text: Express transport apparently without a dining car

parts.words: Express transport apparently without a dining car
parts.note: an express is a quick service, but read another way it is one where passengers go without food

explanation.surface: Complaining that an express has no restaurant carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: To fast is to go without food, so a train with no dining car is 'apparently' fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a quick, rapid railway service.

clue.text: The era of distinctive dress? Rubbish!

parts.note: garb is clothing, especially of a distinctive kind
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Dismissing a period known for its peculiar fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'the age of garb', so the two pieces are joined in the order GARB then AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is refuse, waste, or worthless talk.

clue.text: … which he might have entered upon his table

definitions.text: … which he might have entered upon his table

parts.words: which he might have entered upon his table
parts.note: continuing the previous clue: the Victorian compiler of railway timetables would have listed such an express

explanation.surface: A continuation: the express of the previous clue might appear in this man's tables.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 14-down. George Bradshaw published Britain's railway timetables, and 'Bradshaw' came to mean the timetable itself.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bradshaw compiled the standard Victorian railway timetable.

clue.text: Archbishop at the Zoo?

parts.note: a church title for a senior archbishop, which at the zoo would instead mean an ape or monkey

explanation.surface: Picturing a senior churchman visiting the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Primate of All England is the Archbishop of Canterbury; at the zoo the same word means an ape or monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is a chief archbishop and also a member of the order of apes and monkeys.

clue.text: The faithful servant who keeps what he's got?

definitions.text: The faithful servant who keeps what he's got?

parts.words: The faithful servant who keeps what he's got?
parts.note: a long-serving household servant, read literally as one who holds on to his possessions

explanation.surface: Describing a loyal old family servant who never lets anything go.
explanation.walkthrough: An old retainer is a long-serving servant; the question reads the title as someone who retains things.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a servant attached to a household, and literally one who keeps hold of things.

clue.text: Skill needed to make 0 speech

definitions.meaning: to make a speech, the 0 being a scanning slip for the word a

explanation.surface: Saying that public speaking takes talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The '0' in the held clue is a scanning slip for 'a'. Address in the older sense of dexterity or tact; as a verb it means to speak to a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Address is an old word for adroitness, and to address a meeting is to speak to it.

clue.text: Overtasked when put through a sieve

explanation.surface: Someone feeling pushed through the mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Strained means stretched to the limit, and also filtered through a mesh.

clue.text: Tidy kind of cattle

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen or bovine animals

explanation.surface: Describing a well-kept breed of livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, surviving in 'neatsfoot oil' and 'neat's tongue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means orderly, and is also an old collective term for oxen and cows.

clue.text: Drink like a fish

definitions.meaning: to drink alcohol heavily and habitually
a small shark found in British waters, so it is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: The familiar phrase for heavy boozing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the idiom 'drink like a fish'; split, it gives tope, to drink heavily, and tope, a small shark.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink to excess, and the tope is also a small shark.

clue.text: Petals arranged in folds

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Flower petals laid in creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleats are folds pressed into fabric.

clue.text: Angular bit of building of sound cash value

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a coin is a piece of cash with a face value

explanation.surface: A piece of masonry described as financially sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it tells you a word is pronounced like COIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoin is an external corner stone of a building.

clue.text: Traces erratic course down a slippery slope

indicators.note: erratic suggests wandering, irregular movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tracks wandering down an icy hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is a famous ice toboggan course at St Moritz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run is an icy toboggan track, a course down a slope.

clue.text: Elevated replacement for rapid use

indicators.note: replacement, read as placing again, says the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Something lifted as a quick substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised up means lifted to a higher position.

clue.text: Eastern court designed for comfort

definitions.meaning: an Ottoman council of state or audience chamber

explanation.surface: A luxurious hall in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Divan first meant a Turkish council or court, then the cushioned seat around its walls, then a couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan was an Ottoman council chamber, and is now a low couch made for lounging.

clue.text: Make sure as sure

parts.note: taken as written
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A tautology: to make sure is to be as sure as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, to establish.
